units.translation: And some malevolent god sets you to devise sufferings.
So that I made them, who were before foolish, wise.
There indeed Zeus makes you wise.
So that you may not make the citizens ill-hearted.
Ares, making true the curse of his father.
Making the time long again.
Making the fortunate man, without justice, obscure.
Making the hair wild.
Do not make the path enviable by spreading garments.
Shame makes words blind.
For the son of Leto makes me dishonored.
You made Troy, the city of Ilus, cityless.
You persuaded the Fates to make mortals immortal.
I go, so that I may make the common good favorable.
Let them make the bridegrooms gracious by laws.
He will make the land shady.
Making the wild land tamed.
I will make him a corpse.
The Argive goddess made the woman a cow.
Having made oaths.
Make more toil.
And will you give me a pledge before all time?
What name then will mortals give them?
And they cast a kindly vote.
Nor did they cast a vote with the men.
And let the singers make a song of good omen at the altars.
They cast votes for the man-slaying destruction of Ilium into the bloody urn, not divided.
Be willing to grant this favor to her and that to me.
They made an unexpected evil.
May Zeus, who allots all things, never set power opposed to my will.
But he, always wrathful, having made his mind unbending.
Let us make a careful and deep-counseling thought.
For I will make the affairs of my masters fall out well.
They made prayers and ancestral omens and maiden life as nothing.
Look upon your city, which you once made well-loved.
Having made her own child her husband.
We will make the all-destroying god, the heavy avenger, our housemate.
